lines.say: Why does your face go so red when you lift heavy?
First, you hold your breath and brace.
That squeezes your chest and makes your blood pressure shoot up.
In one study, lifters' blood pressure averaged over three hundred during heavy leg presses.
Blood gets backed up in your head and face.
Second, your body heats up, so vessels in your skin open to dump heat.
For most people it's harmless and fades in minutes. Heart or blood pressure problems? Ask your doctor first.
Next time: why fit people sweat more.
